title: Tooling: 4.78x faster exact bounded quadratic-code replay
body:
The historical quadratic-code rank checker rebuilds large XOR-permutation masks for every row. This tooling improvement adds an opt-in per-replay geometry-mask cache. The original benchmark at `d84d3b950127ff9252e5c059a629bb654500192a` measured the unchanged 4,096-row t=6 workload at **87.66 s → 18.36 s (4.78×)** on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.14.6: three alternating fresh-process pairs, with all six complete receipts byte-identical. This is historical workload timing, not a new measurement of the refreshed dependency closure or integer multiplication.

Only `research/cube-xor-replay/` and its focused Linux workflow are added relative to current main. The source generators, elimination, row order, stopping rule, certificates, selected frontier and `upstream/` retain their current-main state. No new kappa or impossibility result: the t=6 rank lower bound is 3,088 and positive deficit remains **not excluded**.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -I -O -B research/cube-xor-replay/verify.py
```

Python 3.10+, standard library only, in a fresh process/checkout without `.pyc` files. `-B` prevents cache writes but does not disable cache reads. Expected:

```text
PASS_CUBE_XOR_VERIFICATION rows=4324 coefficients=8596927616 t6_rank=3088 t6_excluded=false
```

For the accelerated workload alone: `python3 -I -B research/cube-xor-replay/replay.py --case t6`. Full differential verification also executes the original permutation, so its runtime differs from accelerated replay.

### Review continuation and compatibility

The requested full differential/certificate comparison now completes at both the reviewed original head and current head `4ba229532a76516e5f6f5befc1d6d9dc4834f6f9`. Exact local CPython 3.12.12 runs took 118.575 s and 105.254 s respectively; each completed both cases and all 17 tests. Current-head validation also passes all nine inherited cube tests with the cached backend, all 38 effective Git/SHA256 pins, selected-record integrity, and whitespace checks. Separate AI-assisted source/coverage review found no substantive issue and checked sensitivity of the source and compatibility guards.

The branch incorporates canonical main `ffbd90dd90dbe0055464f3a1411b25a3a4fdc6b8`, priority revision 5. Three changed transitive imports would otherwise reject the integration. A separately authenticated `COMPATIBILITY.json` records exactly those three versions with an explicit path allowlist and predecessor binding. Their changed methods are outside this replay's called path. Original `SOURCES.json`, `EXPECTED-T6.json`, `BENCHMARK.json`, `VALIDATION.json`, `CLAIM.json`, cached permutation and coverage verifier remain unchanged. The complete post-integration replay preserves the scientific receipts.

[Detailed delta and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4ba229532a76516e5f6f5befc1d6d9dc4834f6f9/research/cube-xor-replay/FOLLOWUP.md) · [Canonical continuation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2884). The linked PR follow-up comment records exact logs and live CI status. The historical [Linux job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38441043779/job/115447388058) passed the complete command on its historical PR merge ref; it is separate from [CI for the updated head](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38866849901).

### Evidence and limits

Direct old/new integer equality covers every generated row, including dependent rows: **4,324 rows / 8,596,927,616 binary coefficients**. Both the complete historical t=3,4,5 certificate and full bounded t=6 receipt remain byte-identical. Only geometry masks are cached; input guards still run on warm hits. The written equivalence argument covers every valid power-of-two row width.

The 17 tests include exhaustive small rows, basis/index pairs, seed-94 dense controls, high coordinates, incomplete screens, source/fixture/manifest corruption, and offline relocation. A common column permutation preserves rank and independent-row indices but changes the witness stream; complete receipt comparison rejects it. Dropped rows and corrupt masks are detected.

No new benchmark, full `make verify`, selected native cold replay, supplier admission, Lean or full multiplication theorem is claimed. Generic Python-loader hardening is an explicitly separate next question. Maintainer incorporation and review-ledger disposition remain separate actions.

Historical research base: `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`; original submission base: `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`; cube source: `d55bcd62ceb8f322bcf311a5a66e94c3ac7724f0`. OS seed 94, verification-engineering track. Current overlap refresh covers 491 open PRs and 1,535 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings at 2026-10-16 07:21–07:22 UTC; this continues the existing contribution. PR667 logarithms, PR752 quadratic-affine products, PR898 Leech lanes and PR976 joint-frame rank remain distinct and credited.

Credit **Douglas R. Colkitt** for the original family, permutation, audit and certificate. Contribution and follow-up by **Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, including implementation, mathematical/source audit and testing; no independent human review claimed.
